A relatively calm period of isolated to scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms will persist through Wednesday with coverage
higher over Guam. Very light winds may allow island effect showers
and isolated thunderstorms to develop for all islands, though likely
not too intense due to low level divergence and only moderate 
precipitable water values. Westerlies over Guam may limit development
or push any showers that develop offshore as was seen today. By
Wednesday, moist and unstable air from Invest 95W may allow for
heavier island effect showers and isolated thunderstorms depending on
upper level cloud coverage. Wednesday night through sometime 
Thursday, the monsoon tail of 95W may bring numerous locally heavy 
showers and isolated thunderstorms to the Marianas, with models
indicating higher chances currently over Guam and Rota. Models
currently show widespread 1 to 2 inches for this event but higher
totals will be possible in heavier, training showers. This will be
monitored closely over the next day in case a Hydrologic Outlook or 
Flash Flood Watch needs to be issued. Gusty winds will also be
expected with any thunderstorms. By late Thursday, dry conditions may
return before a new monsoon surge potentially moves into the region
over the weekend.

Marine...
Combined seas around 4 feet will gradually increase through the 
week, reaching as high as 8 to 9 feet due to an increase in 
westerly swell. Light to gentle northwesterlies will become 
southwesterly around midweek, increasing to moderate to fresh for 
the last half of the week. An unsettled, but disorganized monsoon 
pattern continues to bring periods of scattered showers and 
isolated thunderstorms mainly to Guam over the next couple of 
days, potentially becoming numerous with locally heavy showers
possible sometime Wednesday.

For coastal surf, there will be a moderate risk of rip currents 
along west-facing reefs for the next few days. Models and buoys 
indicate north- and south-facing reefs are below 5 feet. The risk may
reach high along west- facing reefs around midweek as a west swell 
builds in. There will be a moderate risk of lightning for Guam 
beginning Tuesday and lasting the whole week.

Tropical Systems...
A developing monsoon disturbance, Invest 94W, is centered northeast 
of Luzon near 21N132E and is currently the subject of a Tropical 
Cyclone Formation Alert by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC). 
This means that 94W is expected to become a significant tropical 
cyclone (Tropical Depression) within the next 24 hours. 94W is 
currently moving slowly northwest. Latest satellite data shows a 
broad, elongated Low-Level Circulation Center (LLCC) obscured by 
persistent convection south through west of the center. Since 
conditions remain conducive to development, Invest 94W is expected to
slowly strengthen as it moves northwest, possibly moving out of the 
Guam Area of Responsibility (AOR) within the next 24 hours. 

For more information on Invest 94W and the TCFA, see bulletins 
issued by JTWC under WMO headers ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

A weak monsoon disturbance, Invest 95W, is found east-southeast of 
Guam, northeast of Weno, Chuuk, near 12N154E. Invest 95W is 
currently rated sub-low, meaning development is not expected for the
next few days. Latest ASCAT analysis shows a weak circulation with 
light winds near the center and stronger environmental winds farther 
south within a monsoon surge across Chuuk State through northeast of
Pohnpei. Invest 95W looks to slowly move toward the north-northwest 
over the next few days, with little development expected until after 
the middle of the week.

Eastern Micronesia...
The monsoon trough is producing a surge to the southeast of Invest 
95W, centered northwest of Pohnpei, and will continue to influence 
the pattern for mainly Pohnpei through Tuesday afternoon. As 95W
slowly moves north-northwest, it will pull the monsoon trough farther
north, allowing the surge to weaken near Pohnpei. This will result in
decreasing convection for the island over the next 24 hours, with
only isolated showers expected for Pohnpei by Tuesday afternoon. For
Kosrae, mostly isolated showers over the next few days. However, a
little surge in convection is expected there this evening, near
midnight, that will bring low-end scattered showers to the island
until early Tuesday morning. Majuro looks to remain dry through at
least the end of the week.

For the marine environment, light to gentle winds are expected for 
Kosrae and Majuro through the period, with seas of 3 to 4 feet. At 
Pohnpei, gentle to moderate winds are expected to weaken, becoming
light to gentle Tuesday afternoon. Combined seas of 4 to 6 feet will
subside to between 3 and 4 feet around Thursday.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows isolated showers across Palau and Yap. 
Scattered showers are seen over Weno, but numerous showers are seen 
across portions of Chuuk State to the north and west of Weno.
